articles.excerpt: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should. articles.summary: Ladybird publie sa première version alpha, qui permet d'installer le navigateur sur macOS ou Linux sans le compiler soi-même. Le projet implémente lui-même la plupart de ses composants principaux (analyse HTML, moteur CSS, mise en page, JavaScript, WebAssembly) et n'utilise que quelques bibliothèques externes, comme HarfBuzz, Skia, ffmpeg et SQLite. articles.excerpt: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-133968 Project MONAI MONAI Label Path Traversal Vulnerability CVE-2026-134624 N-able Mail Assure (SpamExperts) Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability…

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront now supports HTTP/2 connections to custom origins and VPC origins. HTTP/2 lets CloudFront send many requests over fewer connections to your origin. This means fewer connections and TLS handshakes for your origin to handle, which improves performance for API and agentic workloads, such as AI agents calling MCP servers or mobile and web apps calling backend APIs. Until now, CloudFront connected to origins only over HTTP/1.1, which handles one request at a time per connection. When traffic spiked, for example when an AI agent made many tool calls at once, CloudFront had to open more origin connections. Each new connection added latency and load. With HTTP/2, those requests share connections, so your origin does less work and responds faster. HTTP/2 is also supported for WebSocket connections that support extended CONNECT. If your origin doesn't support HTTP/2, CloudFront automatically falls back to HTTP/1.1, so you don't need to change anything on your origin. HTTP/2 to origins is available from all CloudFront edge locations. There is no additional cost for using HTTP/2 to origins. To learn more, visit Origin HTTP version in the CloudFront Developer Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon CloudFront prend désormais en charge les connexions HTTP/2 vers les origines personnalisées et les origines VPC, ce qui permet d'envoyer plusieurs requêtes sur moins de connexions. Selon l'annonce, cela réduit la charge et la latence côté origine, notamment pour les charges de travail API et les agents IA, et l'utilisation reste sans frais supplémentaires. Si l'origine ne supporte pas HTTP/2, CloudFront revient automatiquement à HTTP/1.1, sans modification requise.

articles.excerpt: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves the client IP address for traffic sent to Network Load Balancer (NLB) endpoints with TLS listeners. You can terminate TLS at your NLB and still see the original client IP address in your application. This means you can apply security groups, geo-blocking, rate limiting, fraud detection, audit logging, allowlists, and compliance controls based on the real client IP. Previously, you couldn't add an NLB with a TLS listener to an accelerator that had client IP address preservation enabled. You had to choose between terminating TLS at the NLB and seeing the real client IP address. With this launch, you get both. This helps with workloads that need TLS termination at Layer 4, such as non-HTTP TCP protocols, applications that require static or Elastic IP addresses, and high-throughput traffic where a Layer 7 load balancer isn't a fit. To enable this feature, add an NLB with a TLS listener as an endpoint to an accelerator with client IP address preservation setting turned on, the same way you add any NLB. No additional configuration is required! Client IP address preservation for NLBs with TLS listeners is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions, excluding the AWS GovCloud (US) and China Regions. Standard Global Accelerator pricing applies. articles.title: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves client IPs for NLBs with TLS listeners

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the metal size for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances, accelerated by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1x graphics performance compared to G6. Customers can use the metal size of G7 instances to run physical AI simulations, deploy AI agent sandboxes, and accelerate graphics workloads that need direct access to bare metal infrastructure. G7 metal instances enable customers to run specialized workloads that require a custom virtualization stack, hypervisor-level GPU drivers, or licensing-restricted applications. The metal size of G7 instances feature 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 32 GB of memory per GPU and custom Intel Xeon 6 processors. They support 192 virtual CPUs (vCPUs), 768 GiB of system memory, and 700 Gbps of Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking bandwidth. The new metal size is available in the AWS US East (N. Virginia) Region. You can purchase G7 metal instances as On-Demand Instances, Spot Instances, or as part of Savings Plans. To get started, use the AWS Management Console , AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the G7 instance page .
articles.summary: AWS annonce la disponibilité générale de la taille metal pour les instances Amazon EC2 G7, équipées de 8 GPU NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 Go par GPU) et de processeurs Intel Xeon 6 personnalisés. Elle offre jusqu'à 4,6 fois la performance d'inférence IA et jusqu'à 2,1 fois la performance graphique de la génération G6, avec 192 vCPU, 768 Gio de mémoire et 700 Gbit/s de bande passante EFA. Disponible dans la région US East (Virginie du Nord), elle cible la simulation d'IA physique, les bacs à sable d'agents IA et les charges nécessitant un accès direct au bare metal.

articles.excerpt: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use. With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. For new clusters, select a supported Aurora MySQL engine version and set your maximum capacity up to 384 ACUs. For existing clusters on Platform Version 4, simply modify the cluster to update the maximum capacity setting (and the engine version if needed). There will be no downtime if your database is already on Platform Version 4. For existing clusters on older platform versions, upgrade to Platform Version 4 through a pending maintenance action. 384 ACU support is available for Aurora MySQL versions 3.14 and 8.4.10, running on Platform Version 4. To…
articles.summary: Amazon Aurora Serverless prend désormais en charge une capacité maximale de 384 ACU (Aurora Capacity Units) pour Aurora MySQL, soit une hausse de 50 % par rapport à la limite précédente de 256 ACU. Chaque ACU correspond à environ 2 GiB de mémoire, ce qui permet d'atteindre 768 GiB de mémoire par base de données, avec mise à l'échelle automatique jusqu'à zéro lorsque la charge se termine. La fonctionnalité est disponible pour les versions 3.14 et 8.4.10 d'Aurora MySQL sur la Platform Version 4.
articles.title: Amazon Aurora serverless for MySQL now supports up to 384 ACUs

articles.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker Studio now provides a native developer experience for Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, enabling data scientists to submit distributed training jobs, deploy models, and monitor workloads through a visual interface on HyperPod clusters orchestrated with Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). SageMaker HyperPod is a purpose-built infrastructure for distributed training and fine-tuning of foundation models at scale, designed to reduce infrastructure management overhead. Submitting training jobs and deploying custom models on HyperPod at scale requires familiarity with kubectl and authoring Kubernetes manifests, creating operational burden for data scientists who prefer to work in an interactive development environment. With this launch, data scientists can now submit distributed PyTorch and Ray training jobs and deploy models from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon S3, or Amazon FSx, through single-page forms with a live YAML preview in SageMaker Studio. Compute configurations in the forms provide reusable resource presets that data scientists select when submitting training jobs or deploying models, eliminating manual compute entry. Metrics and logs are embedded directly in the detail pages, powered by HyperPod Observability and Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, surfacing Kubernetes conditions and events, CloudWatch logs, and embedded metrics so data scientists can diagnose workloads without leaving their environment. For teams managing multiple…
articles.summary: Amazon SageMaker Studio permet désormais de soumettre des tâches d'entraînement distribué et de déployer des modèles sur les clusters SageMaker HyperPod orchestrés avec Amazon EKS, via une interface visuelle. Les formulaires proposent des configurations de calcul réutilisables et un aperçu YAML en direct, dispensant les data scientists de manipuler kubectl et les manifestes Kubernetes. Les métriques et journaux sont intégrés aux pages de détail pour diagnostiquer les charges de travail sans quitter l'environnement.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker Studio now supports training job submission and model deployment for SageMaker HyperPod clusters

articles.excerpt: AI agents in Amazon Connect Customer can now populate fields of a step-by-step guide for contact center agents during live customer interactions. With step-by-step guides, managers can design forms and other user interfaces for common workflows, such as rebooking a trip or submitting a claim. Now, AI agents can fill in a guide when it first loads and suggest updates during live conversations, saving time and improving data accuracy. When contact center agents speak to customers, they spend valuable time recording the information they need to solve the customer's problem in a step-by-step guide. For example, when a traveler calls an airline to change her flight, the agent might record her booking reference, dates of travel, and seat preferences. Now, Connect Customer's AI agents can automatically suggest and populate information like this, based on the context of the conversation. Human agents can review each suggestion, accept or reject suggestions individually or in bulk, and make any edits before submitting. The agent can focus on the customer and the problem at hand rather than on manual data entry. You can use AI agents with step-by-step guides in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more and get started, see step-by-step guides in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.
articles.summary: Amazon Connect Customer permet désormais aux agents IA de remplir automatiquement les champs d'un guide étape par étape destiné aux agents de centre de contact, pendant les interactions en direct, et de suggérer des mises à jour au fil de la conversation. Les agents humains peuvent accepter ou rejeter chaque suggestion, individuellement ou en bloc, et les modifier avant de soumettre. La fonctionnalité est offerte dans neuf régions AWS, dont Canada (Centre).
articles.title: Amazon Connect Customer AI agents now fill in step-by-step guides

articles.excerpt: AWS CodeDeploy can now suspend Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes during EC2 in-place deployments to Auto Scaling groups. CodeDeploy is a fully managed service that automates application deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises servers, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon ECS services. This launch helps prevent scaling activities from terminating or replacing instances while CodeDeploy is updating them, which can cause a deployment to fail. You can choose to suspend any combination of these processes (Terminate, AZRebalance, InstanceRefresh, and ScheduledActions) on a deployment group, or on a single deployment. CodeDeploy suspends the processes you choose before it deploys and resumes them when the deployment succeeds, fails, or is stopped, so you don't need custom scripts to suspend and resume processes during deployments. A setting on the deployment group applies to every deployment in that group, including deployments that your existing pipelines start. You can configure this feature by using the CodeDeploy console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or AWS SDKs. This feature is available in all AWS Regions , including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see Suspending Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes during deployments in the AWS CodeDeploy User Guide , or visit the AWS CodeDeploy product page .
articles.summary: AWS CodeDeploy peut désormais suspendre des processus Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling pendant les déploiements in-place sur des groupes Auto Scaling, afin d'éviter que des événements de mise à l'échelle terminent ou remplacent des instances en cours de mise à jour. Les processus sont suspendus avant le déploiement puis repris à la fin, qu'il réussisse, échoue ou soit arrêté, et la fonctionnalité est offerte dans toutes les régions AWS, y compris GovCloud et Chine.
articles.title: AWS CodeDeploy now supports suspending Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes

articles.excerpt: Amazon Inspector has expanded its vulnerability management capabilities with runtime reachability analysis for findings originating from Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances. Previously, Inspector reported every vulnerability found in a resource, including packages that were never used by applications. Security teams had to manually assess which vulnerabilities actually posed risk in their deployed environments. Now, Inspector automatically identifies which vulnerabilities are potentially reachable by analyzing package placement in container images and process activity on EC2 instances. With runtime reachability analysis, you can focus remediation efforts on vulnerabilities that matter most to your security posture. For container images, Inspector determines whether a vulnerable package is within your application's dockerfile paths defined by WORKDIR, ENTRYPOINT, or CMD instructions. For EC2 instances, Inspector identifies whether a vulnerable package was observed running as a process during the most recent scan. For EC2, customers must use the Inspector VM Scanner for agent-based scanning to get this capability. This helps organizations managing large container fleets or complex applications prioritize remediation by distinguishing between vulnerabilities that are potentially reachable versus those in unused dependencies, reducing noise and enabling development and security teams to work more efficiently.…
articles.summary: Amazon Inspector ajoute l'analyse de accessibilité à l'exécution pour les constats provenant d'Amazon ECR et des instances Amazon EC2. L'outil détermine automatiquement quelles vulnérabilités sont potentiellement atteignables, en analysant l'emplacement des paquets dans les images de conteneurs (WORKDIR, ENTRYPOINT, CMD) et l'activité des processus sur les instances EC2. Pour EC2, l'utilisation de l'Inspector VM Scanner en mode agent est requise.
articles.title: Amazon Inspector expands runtime reachability analysis for ECR and EC2 findings

articles.excerpt: AWS Systems Manager Automation now lets you create custom workflows (runbooks) that can automate operational tasks across Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and AWS resources. Automation helps you make changes safely at scale, such as remediating misconfigurations or cleaning up idle resources. Runbooks can roll out in controlled batches, pause for approval, and stop if errors pass a threshold. Instead of maintaining separate tools and credentials for each cloud, teams can now author and execute runbooks from a single place. Six new runbook actions call Azure and Google Cloud APIs, check a resource's state, and wait for operations to finish without custom code. You can target Azure resources by subscription, region, resource group, resource type, and tag. Google Cloud resources can be targeted by project, zone, asset type, and label. For more complex logic, aws:executeScript now includes Azure and Google Cloud Python SDKs and gets short-lived credentials from your Systems Manager Cloud Connector, so you don't store secrets in runbooks. For example, you can stop tagged development virtual machines outside business hours or fix storage buckets that don't meet your security policy. To get started, use the AWS-provided runbooks that install the SSM Agent or the Amazon Inspector agent on your Azure or Google Cloud virtual machines, or create your own custom workflow. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where you can create a Systems Manager Cloud Connector. To learn…
articles.summary: AWS Systems Manager Automation permet désormais de créer des runbooks qui automatisent des tâches opérationnelles sur Azure, Google Cloud et AWS, avec des déploiements par lots, des approbations et un arrêt en cas d'erreurs répétées. Six nouvelles actions de runbook appellent les API Azure et Google Cloud, et aws:executeScript intègre les SDK Python de ces deux fournisseurs avec des identifiants temporaires obtenus via le Cloud Connector.
articles.title: AWS Systems Manager Automation now automates operational tasks in Azure and Google Cloud

articles.excerpt: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now lets customers search across multiple instance types and AWS Regions in a single search, making it easier to find and reserve the capacity their ML workloads need. With Capacity Blocks for ML, customers can reserve accelerated compute instances such as Amazon EC2 P6-B300, P6-B200, and Trn2 instances, for a future start date and for up to 6 months. Until now, customers looking to buy Capacity Blocks had to run a separate search for every instance type and Region combination. Starting today, customers can use a single search in the AWS Management Console to look for Capacity Blocks across multiple instance types and Regions, making it easier to secure capacity without repeated searches. Customers can also programmatically search for capacity across multiple instance types within a Region with a single API call using DescribeCapacityBlockOfferings. This feature is available for all Instance Capacity Blocks in AWS Regions where EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML are offered. For a complete list of supported regions, refer to Capacity Blocks documentation . To get started, visit the Capacity Blocks page in the Amazon EC2 console .
articles.summary: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML permettent désormais de rechercher en une seule requête plusieurs types d'instances et plusieurs régions AWS, au lieu de faire une recherche distincte pour chaque combinaison. La recherche est disponible dans la console AWS et, pour les types d'instances d'une même région, via un appel API unique (DescribeCapacityBlockOfferings).
articles.title: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now supports search across multiple instance types and AWS Regions

articles.excerpt: Open models like Gemma 4 from Google DeepMind are a great option to keep your data local. But how can a local AI model integrate with on-premises data? AlloyDB Omni , Google’s 100% PostgreSQL-compatible database that runs anywhere, now integrates with locally hosted large language models (LLMs). With AlloyDB Omni, you can build agentic experiences on your own infrastructure and on your own terms. Whether it’s in the cloud, in your datacenter, or even on your laptop, you can have data plus AI anywhere. AlloyDB Omni packs powerful, built-in AI, including the same ScaNN indexing technology powering Google Search. When you pair AlloyDB Omni with a model, you can store vector embeddings at scale; search them semantically; and even query the database using natural language. articles.summary: Google annonce que AlloyDB Omni, son édition de base de données compatible PostgreSQL déployable n'importe où, peut désormais se connecter à des modèles de langage locaux comme Gemma 4 et Qwen3.8. Les appels au serveur de modèle se font directement depuis SQL, ce qui garde les données, les requêtes et les réponses dans l'environnement de l'utilisateur. L'extrait présente aussi des fonctions de stockage de vecteurs et de recherche sémantique.
articles.title: Data + AI Anywhere: AlloyDB Omni integration with local models

articles.excerpt: As the scale of global communications grows larger and larger, enterprise platforms must process billions of interactions with customers across a complex network of touchpoints without breaking them. A prime example is Sinch , one of the world’s leading cloud communications and customer engagement (CPaaS) companies, which processes billions of customer interactions, SMS routing events, voice calls, and transactional messages. Managing massive international messaging traffic brings significant architectural challenges, so Sinch built a distributed, multi-cloud data footprint across AWS and GCP, with separate Snowflake instances running in the EU, US, and Australia. Resource spikes and…
articles.summary: Sinch, entreprise de communications cloud (CPaaS) qui traite des milliards d'interactions clients, a migré son entrepôt de données d'entreprise de Snowflake vers Google BigQuery avec l'aide de Google Cloud Professional Services. L'objectif était d'éliminer les silos de données entre ses instances Snowflake en Europe, aux États-Unis et en Australie, de réduire les pics de facturation mensuels et de préparer une plateforme prête pour l'IA.
articles.title: How Sinch modernized its enterprise data warehouse from Snowflake to BigQuery to power AI

articles.excerpt: A teen girl accused of planning to kill a child at her former Winnipeg elementary school was radicalized online and had a romantic fantasy about an American school shooter, a court heard before the teen was granted bail last week.
articles.summary: Une adolescente de 14 ans accusée d'avoir planifié de tuer un enfant dans son ancienne école primaire de Winnipeg aurait été radicalisée en ligne et aurait entretenu un fantasme romantique à l'égard d'un tireur scolaire américain, selon ce qu'a entendu le tribunal. articles.excerpt: London, Ont., police have solved a cold case involving the murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy, who was found strangled in 1968 after a work shift at a convenience store.
articles.summary: La police de London, en Ontario, a résolu le meurtre de Jackie Dunleavy, une adolescente retrouvée étranglée en 1968 après un quart de travail dans un dépanneur. L'affaire, longtemps non résolue, a été élucidée grâce à la généalogie génétique.
articles.title: London, Ont., police solve 1968 murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy using genetic genealogy

articles.excerpt: The Natural Gas Infrastructure Act, if passed, would also allow the government to create a separate provincial entity to plan natural gas infrastructure in the province.
articles.summary: Un projet de loi albertain permettrait à la province de créer une société d'État chargée de la transmission du gaz naturel. articles.title: Legislation would enable Alberta to create a Crown corporation for natural gas transmission

articles.excerpt: The two Americans convicted of murdering Quebec entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner Dominique Marchand in Dominica in December 2023 were sentenced on Monday to life in prison without parole.
articles.summary: Deux Américains condamnés pour le meurtre de l'entrepreneur québécois Daniel Langlois et de son conjoint Dominique Marchand, tués à la Dominique en décembre 2023, ont été sentencés lundi à la prison à perpétuité sans possibilité de libération conditionnelle.
articles.title: 2 Americans sentenced to life in prison for murder of Quebec couple in Dominica

articles.excerpt: The Defence Department will top up the budget of the cadet and junior ranger programs to allow weekend training and other activities to continue into the new year, Defence Minister David McGuinty said on Monday.

L'annonce a été faite lundi par le ministre de la Défense, David McGuinty, après l'indignation suscitée par l'annulation de ces activités.

Ils jugent la situation toujours complexe.
articles.title: Ontario, Alberta premiers weigh in on interprovincial trade, say it remains complicated

articles.summary: Montréal est en lice pour accueillir le siège de la Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), et le gouvernement québécois appuie pleinement cette candidature. L'extrait ne précise pas davantage les étapes ou les concurrents du processus.
articles.title: Quebec rallies behind Montreal’s bid for global defence bank headquarters

articles.title: 3 Calgary police officers charged with manslaughter in death of unarmed Blood Tribe man

articles.excerpt: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew wants to know who spied on his father for the RCMP, and why. Documents obtained by CBC News reveal the late Anishinaabe leader Tobasonakwut Kinew was under surveillance in the 1960s, an early target in a countrywide infiltration initiative later dubbed the "Native extremism program."
articles.summary: Le premier ministre du Manitoba, Wab Kinew, veut savoir qui a espionné son père pour la GRC et pourquoi. Des documents obtenus par CBC News révèlent que feu Tobasonakwut Kinew, leader anishinaabe, faisait l'objet d'une surveillance dans les années 1960, figurant parmi les premières cibles d'une initiative d'infiltration à l'échelle du pays, baptisée plus tard « programme d'extrémisme autochtone ».
articles.title: Spying on survivors: Why RCMP watched Wab Kinew's father in the 1960s

digest.text: Nvidia a réintégré Jensen Huang comme PDG une dizaine de jours après sa démission, avec l'implication déclarée de Trump. L'action a bondi, mais des élus américains critiquent et réclament des enquêtes; le New York Times évoque des liens de sa maîtresse avec le renseignement chinois.

Les marchés ont reculé la semaine dernière, le Nasdaq chutant de 10 % sous l'effet des incertitudes sur l'IA. Morgan Stanley juge la baisse excessive, et Taïwan assouplit ses règles d'appels de marge pour stabiliser son marché.

CrowdStrike acquiert Zscaler pour environ 44 milliards de dollars, afin de renforcer sa sécurité réseau face aux cyberattaques amplifiées par l'IA. Le même jour, Bell enquête sur une fuite de données de clients où un pirate aurait utilisé l'IA.

La CISA avertit qu'une faille critique d'exécution de code à distance dans Cisco Expressway est activement exploitée, après la publication d'un exploit. D'autres failles sont aussi exploitées, dont ScreenConnect, un zero-day VMware et Azure API Management, ce qui exige des correctifs rapides.

La Cour supérieure du Québec a jugé le serment au roi obligatoire pour siéger à l'Assemblée nationale, une décision aux conséquences majeures. Paul St-Pierre Plamondon la qualifie d'« énigmatique et problématique ».

Le président de la Fed de New York, John Williams, indique que des taux plus élevés pourraient être nécessaires à terme pour ramener l'inflation à 2 %. Il table sur un rapprochement de la cible en 2027.

Les procureurs généraux de l'Oregon et de la Virginie poursuivent SpaceX et les entreprises de Musk au sujet des images sexuelles générées par Grok. Ils leur reprochent des mesures de sécurité négligées et une promotion trompeuse; la plainte virginienne vise aussi Musk.
